meta.note: 24 SAMPLE questions written for offline demos (?mock=1). These are NOT College Board questions — download the official bank in Settings or run tools/fetch-bank.mjs.

questions.stem:
Chile's Atacama Desert is often called the driest place on Earth: several of its weather stations have never recorded rain. Yet in the rare years when storms do arrive, dormant seeds burst into bloom, briefly carpeting the desert floor with flowers.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.html: The Atacama Desert receives more rain than most people believe.
Although the Atacama Desert is extremely dry, rare rains can trigger sudden blooms there.
Weather stations in the Atacama Desert are unreliable.
Desert flowers cannot survive without frequent storms.

questions.rationale: Choice B is correct: the text establishes the desert's extreme dryness, then contrasts it with the blooms that follow rare storms. The other choices contradict or go beyond the text.

questions.stem:
A study of city parks found that visitors who walked tree-lined paths reported lower stress than those who walked equally long paths beside roads — even when both groups covered the same distance at the same pace. The researchers therefore concluded that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.html: the stress reduction was caused by exercise alone.
walking near roads is more strenuous than walking among trees.
something about the walk's surroundings, not just the walking itself, affected stress.

questions.rationale: Choice C is correct: distance and pace were held constant, so the differing results point to the surroundings. Choice A is contradicted by the design; B and D aren't supported.

questions.stem: A biologist claims that reef fish return to the exact reef where they hatched, navigating by smell. Which finding, if true, would most directly support the biologist's claim?

options.html: Larval fish raised in water scented with their home reef swim toward that scent in a flume, while fish raised in unscented water show no preference.
Adult reef fish are frequently observed far from any reef.
Reef fish populations decline when water temperatures rise.
Many reef fish species have poor eyesight.

questions.rationale: Choice A is correct: it ties the homing behavior directly to smell with a controlled comparison. B and C are unrelated to navigation by smell; D at best rules out vision without supporting smell.

questions.stem:
The engineer's solution was entirely novel: no bridge had ever been anchored that way before.

As used in the text, what does the word "novel" most nearly mean?
questions.rationale: Choice B is correct: "no bridge had ever been anchored that way before" signals that "novel" means new or unprecedented.

questions.stem:
Most planetarium shows present the night sky as seen from Earth. The new show at the Hayden Planetarium, however, begins on Earth only to pull away — carrying viewers past the planets, out of the galaxy, and to the edge of the observable universe before returning home.

Which choice best describes the function of the first sentence?

options.html: It establishes a convention that the rest of the text contrasts with the new show.
It argues that traditional planetarium shows are superior.

questions.rationale: Choice A is correct: the first sentence describes what most shows do so that "however" can introduce how the new show departs from that convention.

questions.stimulus:
Text 1: Some archaeologists argue that cave paintings were primarily religious, created as part of rituals held deep underground.

Text 2: Recent surveys show many paintings sit near cave entrances, in spaces used for everyday shelter — suggesting art-making was woven into daily life rather than reserved for ceremony.
questions.stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?

options.html: By agreeing that ritual was the sole purpose of cave painting
By noting that the paintings' locations complicate a purely ritual explanation
By denying that any cave paintings exist near entrances
By arguing that the paintings are older than previously thought

questions.rationale: Choice B is correct: Text 2's evidence — paintings in everyday spaces near entrances — challenges the deep-underground ritual account without denying that ritual played any role.

questions.stem:
The team expected the alloy to weaken at high temperatures. ______ it grew stronger, a result no existing model predicted.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Choice A is correct: the result contradicts the expectation, so a contrast transition ("Instead") is needed.

questions.stem:
Lichens survive in deserts, on mountaintops, and even inside Antarctic rocks. ______ they are among the first organisms to colonize ground newly exposed by retreating glaciers.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Choice B is correct: colonizing harsh new ground fits the hardiness just described, so "Fittingly" links the ideas. Contrast transitions (A, C) reverse the logic.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Great Green Wall is an African-led project begun in 2007.
  • Its goal is to restore 100 million hectares of degraded land across the Sahel by 2030.
  • As of 2023, roughly 18 million hectares had been restored.
  • Restored land supports farming and provides income for local communities.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize how much work remains to reach the project's goal. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.html: The Great Green Wall, an African-led project, has restored land that now supports farming.
Though 18 million hectares have been restored since 2007, that is still less than a fifth of the 100 million hectares targeted by 2030.
Begun in 2007, the Great Green Wall aims to restore land across the Sahel.
Restored land provides income for local communities across the Sahel.

questions.rationale: Choice B is correct: it sets the progress (18 million) against the goal (100 million), which is exactly the gap the student wants to emphasize. The other choices omit the comparison.

questions.stem:
Each of the observatory's twin telescopes ______ a mirror more than eight meters across.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: Choice B is correct: the subject is "Each," which is singular, so the singular verb "has" agrees with it. "Of the observatory's twin telescopes" is a prepositional phrase, not the subject.

questions.stem:
Marie Tharp's maps of the Atlantic seafloor revealed a great rift ______ that discovery helped confirm the theory of plate tectonics.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: Choice C is correct: two independent clauses meet here, so a semicolon is needed. A comma alone (A) creates a splice; no punctuation (B) creates a run-on.

questions.stem:
______ the marathon's final mile, spectators lined both sides of the course to cheer the runners home.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: Choice B is correct: the spectators line the course "along" the final mile. Choices A, C, and D each create a dangling modifier — the spectators are not the ones running.

questions.stem: If 3x + 5 = 20, what is the value of x?
questions.rationale: Subtract 5 from both sides: 3x = 15. Divide by 3: x = 5. Choice B is correct.

questions.stem: If x + y = 12 and x − y = 4, what is the value of x?
questions.rationale: Adding the equations gives 2x = 16, so x = 8. Choice C is correct.

questions.stem: The line y = kx − 3 passes through the point (2, 7). What is the value of k?
questions.rationale: Substitute the point: 7 = 2k − 3, so 2k = 10 and k = 5.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² + 1. What is the value of f(3)?
questions.rationale: f(3) = 3² + 1 = 9 + 1 = 10. Choice C is correct.

questions.stem: What are the solutions to the equation (x − 3)(x + 5) = 0?
questions.rationale: A product is zero when a factor is zero: x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3; x + 5 = 0 gives x = −5. Choice C is correct.

questions.stem: If 2x+1 = 32, what is the value of x?
What is 20% of 250?
questions.rationale: 20% of 250 = 0.20 × 250 = 50. Choice B is correct.

questions.stem: A student's five quiz scores are 70, 80, 80, 90, and 100. Which statement about the data is true?

options.html: The mean is greater than the median.
The median is greater than the mean.

questions.rationale: The median (middle value) is 80; the mean is 420 ÷ 5 = 84. The mean exceeds the median, so choice A is correct.

questions.stem: A machine fills 240 bottles in 45 minutes at a constant rate. At this rate, how many bottles does it fill in 2 hours?
questions.rationale: 240 bottles per 45 minutes is 16 bottles per 3 minutes, or 320 per hour. In 2 hours: 640. Choice C is correct.

questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle measure 65° and 45°. What is the measure of the third angle?
questions.rationale: Triangle angles sum to 180°: 180 − 65 − 45 = 70. Choice B is correct.

questions.stem: A circle has a circumference of 16π. What is its radius?
questions.rationale: Circumference = 2πr, so 2πr = 16π and r = 8. Choice B is correct.

questions.stem: In right triangle ABC, the right angle is at C, AC = 5, and BC = 12. What is the value of sin A?
questions.rationale: The hypotenuse AB = √(5² + 12²) = 13. sin A = opposite/hypotenuse = BC/AB = 12/13. Choice C is correct.
